newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel hammered by crude, but more buy.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel hammered by crude, but more buy.

text.p: The second day of tumbling crude futures knocked several dollars of NWE fuel oil on Tuesday.
"Crude is killing fuel," said one trader.
The lower numbers have encouraged end-user buying although the general tone was one of restraint.
"Volatile crude is sidelining some players, we need a period of consolidation," said one dealer.

Two NWE high sulphur cracked cargoes traded on Monday. One was at $114.25 cif U.K while the other was at Dec 10 low cif NWE -$1. A cargo, said to be 4-4.2 percent sulphur, available due to problems at a US coking unit, was sold yesterday for Ireland.
"There is now some strength in the market because demand has emerged," said one dealer who thought prices might pick up.
Romania secured a loan for $160 million to buy 1.3 million tonnes of fuel over the winter which should add further support as will thinning Russian fuel.
The low sulphur market was also weaker. There was talk that an NWE was sold into the Med, but there was no confirmation. Physical barrels were pegged close to paper numbers of $131-131.75 fob NWE.
